description: We are a team of students interested in space exploration, technology, coding, and creativity. For the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, we aim to create an engaging and educational project that gives users an exciting astronaut training experience. Our team will work together using coding, research, design, and teamwork to build a creative and innovative solution.
summary: STORM WATCH is an interactive space education platform that transforms the challenges of Mars exploration into an engaging, hands-on learning experience for young explorers. It combines a 3D Mars colony explorer, an interactive resource management game and educational NASA research to simulate the realities of sustaining a human mission at Jezero Crater. The platform challenges players to keep a crew of four astronauts alive for a 30-day mission by managing essential resources, including oxygen, water, food and energy, while making decisions that directly affect mission survival. By combining immersive exploration with decision-based gameplay, STORM WATCH addresses the gap between simply learning about space mission outcomes and understanding the complex decisions behind them. Its purpose is to make space science more accessible, encourage critical thinking and develop resource-management skills. Ultimately, STORM WATCH aims to inspire the next generation of space explorers by turning complex planetary science into an interactive learning experience.
details:
STORM WATCH — JEZERO OUTPOST is an interactive Mars mission education platform designed to help young learners understand the challenges of human exploration beyond Earth. It combines a 3D Mars colony explorer, NASA space research and a resource management game to create an engaging mission simulation.

Players take responsibility for a crew of four astronauts at Jezero Crater and must manage essential resources, including oxygen, water, food and energy, throughout a 30-day mission. Every decision affects the crew's ability to survive and maintain the colony. The platform also presents educational information about space weather, radiation and the challenges of living on Mars, using archived NASA research data.

Developed using JavaScript, HTML, CSS and Three.js with Vite, the project runs directly in a web browser without requiring downloads or an account. We used VS Code, Node.js, GitHub and Vercel during development.

Our creative approach combines 3D exploration with decision-based gameplay, turning complex space science into an accessible learning experience. We considered educational value, user accessibility, performance and realistic resource constraints. Our goal is to inspire curiosity, critical thinking and better understanding of future Mars missions.
